caption:
Cursor's new AI just stopped writing code — and users are shipping 6x more 🤖

Most AI coding tools quit the second you close your laptop. Cursor's new Projects feature doesn't: a coordinator agent plans the work, then hands it to thousands of subagents that keep coding in the cloud.

→ the coordinator only plans and delegates, it never touches code itself
→ subagents do the actual coding and testing, in parallel
→ it keeps running on its own cloud machine after you log off
→ built for work that outlives one chat: features, migrations, big jobs

Would you trust an AI to keep coding while you sleep? 👇

Save this for how it works, and follow @aiplaybooks.daily for daily AI tool news.

captions.facebook:
Cursor just changed how AI coding tools work.

Instead of one AI writing code line by line, Cursor's new Projects feature uses a coordinator agent that only plans and delegates. It hands the actual coding to thousands of subagents running in the cloud — so the work keeps going even after you close your laptop.

The result: people who mainly use Projects are merging 6x more pull requests than before.

Would you let an AI keep working on your project while you're away, or do you like watching it happen? Let us know below.
